title: FLEX(-) Bacterial DNA Extraction Protocol for Nanopore and Hybrid Whole Genomic Sequencing
author: Jack Boulé
materials: Once dry, take the tube/plate off the magnet.
Wait 2-3 min for pellet to reform.

steps.title: Label tubes and collection vessels
steps.instruction: Label a matching set of PowerBead tubes and Lo‑Bind tubes for each isolate using the same sample ID format. Also label the collection vessels (either 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes for ≤48 samples or a 0.8 mL 96‑well PCR plate for >48 samples). Use the appropriate magnet type for the chosen vessel (96‑well plate magnet for PCR plate, standing tube magnet such as ThermoFisher DynaMag for Eppendorfs).

steps.title: Preheat temperature block to 56 °C
steps.instruction: Set a temperature block or water bath to 56 °C and allow it to equilibrate before use.

steps.title: Attach Qiagen vortex adapter
steps.instruction: Attach the Qiagen Vortex Adapter top to a Vortex‑Genie (or equivalent). The adapter holds up to 24 samples; use multiple adapters if processing more than 24 samples.

steps.title: Calculate enzyme and reagent volumes
steps.instruction: Calculate the required amount of each enzyme (e.g., Proteinase K) and each reagent for the planned batch size according to Table 1 (enzymes) and Table 2 (reagents).

steps.title: Thaw Proteinase K and keep cold
steps.instruction: Remove Proteinase K from the freezer, allow it to thaw, and keep it at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Add TE buffer to PowerBead tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot 300 µL of TE buffer into each 0.5 mm glass PowerBead tube.

steps.title: Inoculate tubes with bacterial colonies
steps.instruction: Inoculate each PowerBead tube with isolated bacterial colonies using a heaping 1 µL loop or half of a 10 µL loop, minimizing agar carry‑over. After inoculation, gently spin/rotate the loop in the tube to disperse and homogenize the biomass.

steps.title: Add Sarkosyl and gentle mix
steps.instruction: Pipette 8 µL of 10 % Sarkosyl into each PowerBead tube (use a P10). Slowly pipette up and down 2–3 times; avoid excessive foaming. If foam forms, let it settle and tap the tube gently.

steps.title: Vortex beads for lysis
steps.instruction: Insert the PowerBead tubes into the Qiagen Vortex Adapter with caps facing inward, place the adapter onto the vortex, set speed to 9 (or maximum), and vortex for 5 minutes. If the vortex spins faster than expected, lower the speed to avoid over‑fragmentation.

steps.title: Remove adapter and rack tubes
steps.instruction: Turn off the vortex, remove the adapter top, and place the tubes back onto a rack in their original layout.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and mix
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) into each tube (use a P10) and gently pipette mix up and down 2–3 times.

steps.title: Incubate at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a 56 °C dry incubator or water bath, maintaining the original layout, and incubate for 15 minutes. Then remove from the incubator.

steps.title: Bind DNA with SPRI beads
steps.instruction: Transfer 225 µL of lysate from each PowerBead tube to a 0.8 mL 96‑well plate or 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube (same format as step 1). Add 225 µL of SPRI Select beads (1:1 ratio) to each well/tube. Pipette up and down 3–5 times to achieve homogeneous mixing; insufficient mixing will prevent complete DNA binding.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 225 µL lysate to new vessel

steps.title: Magnet binding and pellet formation
steps.instruction: Place the plate or tubes onto the appropriate magnet (96‑well Illumina Magnet for plates, Thermo DynaMag for Eppendorfs). Allow to sit until the lysate becomes clear and a pellet forms on the side wall (≈3–5 minutes). For Eppendorfs, rotate the tube left and right on the magnet to speed pellet formation.

steps.title: Remove supernatant on magnet
steps.instruction: While the plate/tube remains on the magnet, carefully remove the supernatant with a P1000 set to 1000 µL, avoiding contact with the pellet. If any pellet is aspirated, return it to the well/tube, let sit 2 minutes, then repeat supernatant removal.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL of 80 % ethanol directly onto the pellet, resuspend by pipetting up and down until homogeneous (scrape with tip if needed). Place back on the magnet, allow the pellet to collect, then remove the ethanol supernatant with a P1000 set to 1000 µL.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add another 600 µL of 80 % ethanol onto the pellet, do NOT fully resuspend; simply let the ethanol sit. Place on the magnet, then remove and discard the supernatant with a P1000, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 10 minutes, monitoring to prevent over‑drying (visible cracking). Slight over‑drying is preferable to under‑drying, as residual ethanol contaminates the eluate.

steps.title: Elute DNA with molecular water
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of molecular‑grade water (ddH₂O) directly onto the pellet. If yield is low, the volume may be decreased. Resuspend the pellet fully by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Transfer eluate to Lo‑Bind tube
steps.instruction: Place the tube/plate back onto the magnet, allow the liquid to clear, then transfer the entire 100 µL supernatant to a labeled Lo‑Bind Eppendorf tube. Store the DNA solution at –80 °C (stable up to 10 years).

steps.title: Discard used tubes/plate
steps.instruction: Discard the empty tubes or plate that contain the pellet (DNA is now in the transferred supernatant).

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA using a Qubit Fluorometer: mix 4 µL of eluate with 196 µL of High‑Sensitivity Reagent (follow ONT NO‑MISS protocol for acceptable concentrations).

steps.title: Assess purity with Nanodrop
steps.instruction: Check for contamination with a Nanodrop (or equivalent) and record 260/280 and 260/230 ratios as per ONT NO‑MISS guidelines.

steps.title: Optional fragment length analysis
steps.instruction: Optionally assess fragment length distribution using a Bioanalyzer or Fragment Analyzer according to ONT NO‑MISS recommendations.
